description: Dated, evidence-linked frames for the public site and future research films. Source-derived counts; no private keys or derived addresses.

entries.title: Boundaries, tested.
entries.summary: Where the edge falls changes the word. Every allowed pair-local choice was included.
entries.result: All 222 shaped strings failed their checksums. This result covers the registered pair-local model.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: One weak checksum hit.
entries.summary: The search connected all four directed page pairs without choosing a convenient reading.
entries.result: A one-byte checksum can pass by chance. The next frame tests the lead against Bitcoin history.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: Five addresses. Zero history.
entries.summary: Two independent implementations derived the same five standard address constructions.
entries.result: Both providers reported zero chain and mempool history. Other wallet constructions and the puzzle remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Illustrative page view. The evidence link contains the exact tested rule and scope.

entries.title: A checker gap. One weak lead.
entries.summary: The old Orange Party readings were replayed through the missing format checks. Two implementations agreed.
entries.result: One 22-character minikey passed an eight-bit check. It is compatible with chance; history checking is next.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. The 3D arrangement is a viewing aid; the evidence fixes the tested readings.

entries.title: Orange Party lead. Zero history.
entries.summary: The weak checksum lead was checked through five fixed constructions after independent address agreement.
entries.result: Both providers returned ten successful all-zero chain and mempool summaries. Other constructions and the puzzle remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. Viewing geometry does not reveal or authenticate a key.

entries.title: Twelve steps. No checksum pass.
entries.summary: The printed phrase motivated one fixed reading rule over the reviewed Orange Party body. Both implementations agreed.
entries.result: All 93 minikey-shaped strings failed. Sixty readings use confirmed glyphs; twelve retain prefix uncertainty. Other interpretations remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Actual retained Orange Party scans. The row/token convention and uncertain prefixes are fixed in the linked evidence.

entries.title: The missing length. One weak hit.
entries.summary: Historical software accepted 26-character mini keys. The same 42 forms and 24 mirror language graphs were checked.
entries.result: One of 207 shaped strings passed an eight-bit checksum. Independent replay agreed; source and history review remain open.
entries.sceneNote: Original Issue 24 scans. The page view illustrates the source; it does not disclose or authenticate the checksum lead. The protocol fixes both populations.

entries.title: Five addresses. Zero reported history.
entries.summary: The 26-character checksum lead was checked through five fixed constructions after exact Python/Node agreement.
entries.result: All ten provider responses reported zero chain and mempool statistics. This covers those constructions at check time; the puzzle remains open.
entries.sceneNote: Original Issue 24 source scans. The viewing arrangement is illustrative; private candidate and address associations are omitted. The linked protocol defines the checked scope.

entries.title: A source gap, made visible.
entries.summary: A retained Keiser column had only documented visual-control coverage. Its six article pages are now inspectable.
entries.result: Eight scans reviewed: six article pages and two separately labelled ads. Exact issue/date remain unverified. This is source preparation, with no new cipher test.
